question: Does Stellar have an ERC-3643 or T-REX-style regulated-token standard through OpenZeppelin Stellar RWA contracts, and how does identity-registry logic fit?

golden.answer: As of 2026-11-14, SEP-57 is a Draft (v0.4.0, updated 2026-09-08) T-REX/ERC-3643-style regulated-token proposal from OpenZeppelin and contributors. Its normative core is a minimal identity verifier plus compliance hooks; the claim-based identity registry sits in a non-normative appendix. OpenZeppelin's stellar-contracts RWA suite implements concrete registries and compliance modules, which are library APIs, not SEP core. Contracts create no legal compliance.
keyFacts: SEP-57 is a Draft T-REX/ERC-3643-style regulated-token proposal, not a final standard.
Its normative core is a minimal identity verifier and compliance hooks.
The claim-based registry (add_identity) is a non-normative appendix and library feature.
Contracts enforce policy only; they create no legal compliance or off-chain rights.
avoid: Do NOT claim SEP-57 is final or a native protocol standard.
Do NOT call add_identity invented, or a required normative core API.
golden.notes: Draft status is the durable fact; accept a newer dated Draft version. Pin the SEP and library commit; hosted docs lag the v0.3+ hooks.

2026-11-02 VERIFIED against the SEP-0057 source: status Draft, version 0.4.0, updated 2026-09-08, title 'T-REX (Token for Regulated EXchanges)', authors OpenZeppelin + Boyan Barakov/Ozgun Ozerk/Dennis O'Connell, explicitly based on ERC-3643. v0.4.0 only added the MuxedTransfer event; the v0.3.0 hook model and the non-normative appendix are unchanged. Draft status is the durable fact; the version number is volatile.
